note: These are conversion blueprints organized around observable buying jobs. Discovery confirms fit; this catalog never approves a launch.

archetypes.name: AI / Automation Authority System
archetypes.primaryJTBD: When a buyer knows the workflow is expensive but cannot yet judge the technical approach, I want to make the mechanism and next diagnostic step credible so I can earn a qualified assessment conversation.
buyerHesitations: Will this work with our systems?
Is this a real capability or a fashionable claim?
archetypes.heroPrinciple: Name the expensive workflow, show the operating mechanism, and make the first diagnostic step concrete.
archetypes.motionRule: Use restrained signal movement to explain a system; never use animated dashboards as a substitute for proof.
prohibitedPatterns: AI hype without a specific workflow
disqualifiers: Unverified client data used in examples

archetypes.name: SaaS Launch & Demand System
archetypes.primaryJTBD: When a product is ready for a focused launch but its value is spread across features, I want to turn the product promise into a clear buying path so I can create qualified demos or trials.
buyerHesitations: Is this for a real use case?
How is it different from the tools we already use?
Will switching or adopting it be worth the effort?
archetypes.heroPrinciple: Lead with the use case and decision outcome, then let the product evidence earn the feature detail.
proofRequirements: Security or implementation facts where relevant
archetypes.motionRule: Motion may stage a product flow or reveal a real interface; keep the first meaningful paint and reduced-motion path intact.
prohibitedPatterns: Demo CTA with no qualification context

archetypes.name: Expert Authority System
archetypes.primaryJTBD: When expertise is valuable but difficult to compare, I want to make the point of view, fit, and engagement path legible so the right buyer can start a credible conversation.
buyerHesitations: Is this expertise relevant to my situation?
What happens after the first conversation?
archetypes.heroPrinciple: A precise point of view is the hero; biography and credentials support the decision rather than carrying it.
archetypes.motionRule: Prefer quiet transitions and typographic emphasis; motion must not compete with the argument.
disqualifiers: Offer is only a broad identity exercise

archetypes.name: Creative Portfolio & Inquiry System
archetypes.primaryJTBD: When the work is visually strong but project fit is hard to judge, I want to curate proof and make the inquiry boundary clear so I can attract better-fit briefs.
buyerHesitations: Can they handle our kind of brief?
Can the studio deliver within our constraints?
archetypes.heroPrinciple: Curate a point of view and a small set of relevant work; do not let the portfolio become an unstructured archive.
archetypes.motionRule: Use scroll choreography only where it clarifies the work; provide still, readable alternatives and protect mobile performance.
prohibitedPatterns: Case studies without role or context
disqualifiers: Demand for spectacle without an inquiry path

archetypes.name: High-Trust Lead Engine
archetypes.primaryJTBD: When a buyer must feel safe before sharing context, I want to reduce uncertainty and make the first low-risk step explicit so I can create qualified inquiries without overpromising.
buyerHesitations: What will happen to my information?
Will I be pressured after I inquire?
archetypes.heroPrinciple: Make safety, scope, response expectations, and human contact visible before asking for sensitive information.
archetypes.motionRule: Use minimal motion; clarity, focus order, consent, and calm interaction take priority over atmosphere.
prohibitedPatterns: Sensitive data before purpose is clear
